meta.scene_summary: We are teaching AI to micromanage the world while simultaneously making our hardware too small to run it and our financial advice too confident to be legal.

cooking.headline: Sam Altman is taking AI regulation to the UN
cooking.summary: Sam Altman is heading to the UN Security Council to discuss AI, which is essentially the tech equivalent of bringing your group project to the principal's office. It's hard to tell if he's there to save humanity or just to make sure the AI arms race stays within the company budget.
cooking.plain_english: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman will meet with the United Nations Security Council to discuss the potential risks and regulations concerning artificial intelligence technology.

cooking.headline: Google is teaching AI agents how to micromanage each other
cooking.summary: Google released an orchestrator to help AI agents coordinate, essentially automating the experience of a group project where nobody knows who's in charge. It's a bold strategy to see if giving agents the ability to delegate tasks results in actual work or just a very expensive infinite loop of meetings.
cooking.plain_english: Google has released a tool that allows multiple artificial intelligence agents to work together and manage complex tasks by delegating them to one another.

cooking.headline: Cloudflare finally lets you run Python without the heavy lifting
cooking.summary: Cloudflare now supports Python Workers, meaning you can finally stop pretending you enjoy writing JavaScript just to keep your serverless functions lightweight. It's the perfect update for developers who want to ship code without having to pack a suitcase full of dependencies every time they deploy.
cooking.plain_english: Cloudflare has officially added support for the Python programming language to its serverless computing platform, allowing developers to run Python code directly on their network.

cooking.headline: Heretic decided that AI guardrails are just suggestions meant to be ignored
cooking.summary: The Heretic project is stripping away safety restrictions from LLMs, effectively turning them into unfiltered digital teenagers. It is a bold experiment that treats safety protocols like a group project where you decide to do all the work yourself.
cooking.plain_english: The Heretic project provides methods to remove safety and content restrictions from existing artificial intelligence models.

cooking.headline: Mini-AGI runs on 8GB of VRAM, finally letting your GPU stop complaining about its lack of storage.
cooking.summary: We've spent years believing AGI requires a server farm the size of a small country, but apparently, it just needed a better diet plan. It's like finding out you can run a marathon on a single cup of coffee instead of a full buffet.
cooking.plain_english: A new artificial intelligence model has been developed that can perform complex tasks while using a relatively small amount of computer memory.

cooking.headline: Kev is the latest tiny decision model, because apparently, we aren't satisfied with AI until it's microscopic.
cooking.summary: We're currently in the 'make it smaller' phase of the AI gold rush, which is essentially just developers trying to fit a genius into a shoebox. It's the tech equivalent of trying to see how many clowns you can fit in a car, except the clowns are actually useful.
cooking.plain_english: A small family of decision-making artificial intelligence models has been released that utilizes the Qwen3.5 architecture.

cooked.headline: Amazon just told Meta's new AI agent to stay off the lawn
cooked.summary: Amazon is blocking Meta's new shopping agent, proving that even in the future, your favorite store still hates automated scripts. It turns out that when you build an AI designed to do your shopping, the retailers view it as a bot-driven denial-of-service attack rather than a helpful assistant.
cooked.plain_english: Amazon has implemented measures to prevent Meta's new artificial intelligence shopping assistant from accessing its website to browse or purchase products.

cooked.headline: Raspberry Pi just patched out your hardware upgrade dreams
cooked.summary: Raspberry Pi is actively blocking users from soldering on more RAM, effectively turning a tinkerer's dream into a locked-down black box. It's a bold strategy to prevent people from fixing their own hardware, because heaven forbid your $80 computer actually outlives its original specs.
cooked.plain_english: Raspberry Pi has released a software update that prevents the device from functioning if the original memory chips are replaced with higher-capacity ones.

cooked.headline: The Pi is no longer the DIY king if you can't even swap the RAM
cooked.summary: They've pushed an EEPROM update that bricks your board if it detects unauthorized memory, which is a hilarious way to say 'stop having fun in ways we didn't authorize.' It's like buying a Lego set that refuses to snap together if you try to build something that isn't on the box. More details in the original article.
cooked.plain_english: A new firmware update for the Raspberry Pi 5 intentionally disables the device if the user attempts to upgrade the RAM manually.

cooked.headline: AI chatbots are now essentially confident financial advisors who failed Econ 101
cooked.summary: Financial institutions are testing AI for customer queries, but the models are hallucinating incorrect answers most of the time. It turns out that 'predictive text' is a terrible strategy for managing your life savings.
cooked.plain_english: Large language models frequently provide inaccurate information when asked questions about financial topics.
